content.title: What day does 'The Pitt' come out? A Florida woman is in the cast
content.text: March 27, 2026, 4:40 p.m. ET"The Pitt" is a fictional drama series on HBO Max about frontline healthcare workers in an under-resourced ER.The show's second season follows a real-time format, with each one-hour episode representing one hour of a 15-hour shift.New episodes of "The Pitt" are released on HBO Max every Thursday at 9 p.m. ET.HBO Max's "The Pitt" has been taking the internet by storm with the release of its second season, which has a new episode drop weekly on the streaming platform.The uniquely formatted show is a (reportedly very realistic) fictional drama series that focuses on frontline healthcare workers in a busy and under-resourced emergency room. Each season of the show takes place over one 15-hour shift in the ER, using a real-time format in which one hour-long episode is equivalent to one hour in the shift.The season two premiere garnered more than five million viewers within three days of its release.Although the show is set in Pittsburgh, Tal Anderson, who plays Becca King on the show, is from Florida.Here's how to watch HBO Max's 'The Pitt,' when the season 2 finale will release and what to know about the Floridian actress who plays Becca King.What day of the week does 'The Pitt' drop? When is 'The Pitt' season 2 finale?New episodes of "The Pitt" drop on HBO Max every Thursday at 9 p.m. ET. The season two premiere was released on Jan. 8. The season finale will air on April 16.Who is Tal Anderson? 'The Pitt' actress is from FloridaTal Anderson is an actress from Cape Coral, Florida, who considers herself an advocate for change in Hollywood. Autistic herself, she has played two notable TV characters with autism: an autistic college student on Netflix's "Atypical" and Becca King, the autistic sister of Dr. Mel King on "The Pitt."“I like to play neurodivergent characters,” she told the Fort Myers News-Press. "Because I can portray their perspective — usually from a place of shared, lived experiences. But also, I want those characters to have the opportunity to be played authentically by a neurodivergent actor.“Representation alone, it's important. But when it's authentic — and the character's point of view is more real and less stereotypical — it's more powerful."Her role in the first season of "The Pitt" was a minor one, but her character was expanded for season two, giving Anderson more time on screen.“It's been a crazy journey, you know…” She told the News-Press. “I think 'The Pitt' is the biggest show I've ever been on.”How to watch 'The Pitt' on HBO MaxWatch 'The Pitt' with the Disney bundleNew episodes of "The Pitt" drop on HBO Max every Thursday at 9 p.m. ET.Contributing: Charles Runnells, Fort Myers News-Press & Naples Daily NewsLianna Norman is a trending reporter for the USA TODAY NETWORK-Florida, covering pop culture, rocket launches, Florida wildlife, breaking news and more.
